newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian housing recovery still patchy - industry.
newsitem.headline: Australian housing recovery still patchy - industry.

text.p: Australian building industry groups said on Monday the latest housing finance figures showed the housing industry was unlikely to improve significantly until the September quarter this year.
Figures earlier on Monday showed finance commitments for owner-occupied housing in Australia fell a seasonally-adjusted 6.9 percent by volume to 39,457 dwellings in February.

"The latest housing finance figures indicate the housing recovery is unlikely to become more robust until the September quarter this year," Master Builders Australia national director economics and housing Wilhelm Harnisch said in a statement.
Harnisch said that while the fall was disappointing, it was not unexpected at this stage of the recovery cycle.
"Uncertainty about the job market is holding back home buyers," he said.
"Any suggestion of an interest rate rise would be inappropriate and would simply spook the housing market."
Housing Industry Association Ltd managing director Ron Silberberg agreed that home buyers were still uncertain about the housing market.

"Potential home buyers are remaining cautious and builders are reporting that growth in housing activity is occurring mainly in the multi-unit sector with the market for detached houses still patchy," Silberberg said in a statement.
Real Estate Institute of Australia Ltd president Don Brindley said many areas of the housing market were still to show signs of a recovery.
"What today's housing finance figures reflect is the patchy nature of the current housing recovery," Brindley said.
